html:
Caligula was the third Roman emperor, ruling from 37 to 41 CE, and is remembered as one of the worst. His real name was Gaius; Caligula, "little boot", was the soldiers' nickname for him as a small boy in army boots in his father's camps on the Rhine.

He was the son of the popular general Germanicus and a great-grandson of Augustus, and a grandson of Agrippa. Most of his family died in the purges under Tiberius, but he survived, and when Tiberius died in 37 he was welcomed as emperor.

After a serious illness late in 37 his rule turned harsh. He spent heavily, demanded honours as a god, humiliated senators and killed rivals. He exiled his sister Agrippina and had his relative Ptolemy, king of Mauretania, put to death, which led to the kingdom becoming a Roman province. Many stories about him, such as plans to make his horse a consul, come from hostile writers and may be exaggerated.

He also started useful works, among them the Aqua Claudia aqueduct. He brought an obelisk from Egypt on a giant ship that was later sunk to form the base of the lighthouse at Portus. In January 41 officers of the Praetorian Guard killed him in his palace, and the guard made his uncle Claudius emperor.
